dramatic.state_in: Greg's old-life road knowledge feels concrete enough to trust while current Carrow has changed around it.
dramatic.required_result: Let Sevren's current route expose how accurate old knowledge can still be operationally stale.
dramatic.state_out: Greg accepts he knew the road, not knows it, and writes ASK CURRENT ROUTE.
dramatic.ownership: Sevren owns current route/cart safety; Greg owns historical knowledge and his body.

performance.pressure: Greg's confidence is punctured by infrastructure changes, not false memory.
performance.behavior: Sevren answers current facts without indulging Greg's old map; Greg argues with bridges, catches himself, then considers a future ride through actual body/logistics constraints.
performance.relationship: Sevren treats Greg's strange knowledge as interesting, not sacred.

screenplay: Greg finds Sevren under a courier cart and asks about the north run.
He discovers the toll house burned, timber bridge vanished, lower crossing widened, quarry road changed and bridge traffic rules shifted.
He keeps being factually right about the old road and practically wrong about the current route.
Sevren offers to consider him for a future north ride if load and road permit.
Greg's mind floods with road vibration, getting down, food, rain, crutch storage and other constraints.
He does not build a system; later he records only current road facts and ASK CURRENT ROUTE.

audit.rhythm: SOURCE_WIN: concern list intentionally enacts involuntary accumulation

dramatic.state_in: Greg is useful enough at rehearsal to receive small live roles.
dramatic.required_result: Use a four-line messenger entrance to force coordination of lines, props, movement, listening and recovery.
dramatic.state_out: Greg starts responding inside a scene rather than executing a sequence.
dramatic.ownership: Teren owns prompting/entry correction; scene partners own live responses; Greg owns messenger choices.

performance.pressure: Greg wants four lines to be the task, but everything around them is the task.
performance.behavior: He enters wrong door, mishandles letter timing and anticipates exits, then eventually listens; when he forgets the prop he improvises instead of aborting.
performance.relationship: Theatre gives bounded failure without protecting him from embarrassment.

screenplay: Greg is handed four messenger lines and a prop letter because he is there.
He picks the wrong blue door, traps the letter in his grip and talks to the page.
Repeated runs add handoff timing, pause, exit, actor changes and stage traffic.
A floor click tempts Greg to optimize foot placement; Teren tells him to leave the board.
Later Greg enters without the letter and improvises being lied to instead of stopping.
The actors play it, laugh, reset and keep working.

audit.rhythm: SOURCE_WIN: Again and failed-entry beats are performance timing

dramatic.state_in: External apparatus is set aside; internal directional control is the stronger signal.
dramatic.required_result: Test whether Greg follows a changed direction rather than a prepared target.
dramatic.state_out: He fails the changed cue but RETURNs cleanly, separating directional weakness from general control.
dramatic.ownership: Hessa owns the surprise change; Greg owns report.

performance.pressure: Greg sees apparatus removal as loss until Hessa reframes the evidence.
performance.behavior: Hessa reviews thread attempts and safe-attempt budget; during the internal test she changes direction after setup; Greg reports that the old target wins.
performance.relationship: Hessa uses Greg's desire for clean evidence against his desire for more attempts.

screenplay: The thread frame is gone; Greg challenges the decision.
Hessa reviews all three thread attempts and explains why a fourth is not worth current tolerance.
She marks a target and lets Greg establish a localized alteration.
Then she changes the directional cue away from the prepared mark.
Greg's edge sharpens toward the old mark and he reports the wrong direction.
RETURN works cleanly. Changed-direction question fails; control sequence does not.

dramatic.state_in: Prepared-target bias is known; one direction-first report favored wristward.
dramatic.required_result: Test the opposite direction with no prepared destination.
dramatic.state_out: Greg again reports asymmetry toward the instructed side, raising confidence while remaining subjective.
dramatic.ownership: Hessa owns evidence strength; Greg owns report.

performance.pressure: Greg knows expectation can manufacture confidence.
performance.behavior: He waits through ambiguity and downgrades certainty; Hessa records only instructed-side asymmetry and lack of independent confirmation.
performance.relationship: Shared technical vocabulary makes the scene quieter rather than combative.

screenplay: Blank forearm, no target. Hessa defines elbowward as direction independent of her fingers.
Greg forms a neutral altered region and reports size/shape before direction.
On cue the elbow-side boundary becomes sharper, maybe, while wrist side stays.
Greg says think rather than know when pressed.
RETURN softens the elbow-side distinction first, then the rest.
Hessa records the opposite instructed-direction result without promoting the claim.

dramatic.state_in: Opposite direction-first reports suggest directional ability but need replication.
dramatic.required_result: Repeat wristward under similar conditions and force a claim-threshold decision.
dramatic.state_out: Hessa upgrades narrow directional control to provisionally supported while denying broader implications.
dramatic.ownership: Hessa owns wording threshold; Greg owns sensory report/questions.

performance.pressure: Greg wants one clean sentence of progress after many qualifiers.
performance.behavior: He distrusts the immediacy of the response and reports it anyway; Hessa finally grants stronger wording because the repeated pattern earns it.
performance.relationship: The payoff works because Hessa's standards stayed hard.

screenplay: Hessa announces wristward replication with no prepared target.
Greg forms a neutral region and rates confidence moderate.
On wristward cue the wrist-side edge sharpens quickly; Greg questions the speed rather than hiding it.
Hessa orders sensation report, then RETURN.
The alteration reduces cleanly with no motor or left-side response.
Hessa says directional control is provisionally supported under this narrow condition; Greg allows himself progress without converting it into casting clearance.
